biography: Jacques Thenaers, a name whispered with a mix of anticipation and exasperation in the Giallo garage, hails from the Ardennes region of Belgium. The roar of engines wasn't a distant dream, but a daily reality. His father ran a small karting track, and Jacques practically grew up strapped into a kart. He wasn't an instant prodigy; early races were marked by spectacular crashes and the occasional podium. One particularly memorable incident involved Jacques misjudging a corner and ending up in a farmer's field, much to the amusement of the local spectators. However, his raw talent and relentless determination caught the eye of a local racing school. Progress through the junior formulas was steady, if unspectacular, until a surprise win at Spa in Formula 3 catapulted him into the Giallo program. Now at 26, he is considered a 'rising' talent, but his inconsistency is a constant source of frustration for the team. He possesses flashes of brilliance but struggles to maintain that level across an entire race weekend.
drivingStyle: Thenaers' driving style can be described as 'opportunistic aggression.' He's not afraid to throw the car into corners, relying on instinct and car control to make the move stick. This sometimes pays off handsomely, resulting in breathtaking overtakes and unexpected podiums. However, this aggressive approach can also lead to costly mistakes, tire wear issues, and unnecessary contact with other drivers. Tire management is definitely a weakness, and his ability to handle pressure is directly proportional to how confident he feels at the start of the race. A nervous Thenaers is a slow Thenaers.

rivalries.name: Marco Bellini
rivalries.reason: Bellini, a veteran known for his tactical brilliance, publicly criticized Thenaers' aggressive driving after a controversial incident at Monza where Thenaers' late braking maneuver forced Bellini off the track.

rivalries.name: Anya Petrova
rivalries.reason: Petrova and Thenaers are seen as representing different approaches to racing - calculated precision vs. raw aggression - leading to clashes on and off the track, fueled by competitive fire.

rivalries.name: Ricardo Alvarez
rivalries.reason: Alvarez and Thenaers were teammates in Formula 3 and their rivalry stemmed from battling for the same spot in the team. Alvarez believes Thenaers was favored by team management.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, even if they're full of holes.
Listens to a specific Belgian techno track (a very obscure one) precisely 30 minutes before every race.
Refuses to eat anything green on race days, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "Sometimes, you just gotta send it. Worry about the consequences later."
careerHighlight: Winning the Formula 3 race at Spa-Francorchamps from P10 on the grid in the wet, showcasing his exceptional car control and overtaking prowess.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Monaco Grand Prix in his debut season, costing him a potential podium and severely damaging his reputation within the team.
